data.name: Sharwanand
data.gender_notes: Sharwanand is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Sharwanand is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'sharas' (quencher of desire) and 'anand' (bliss). It refers to the Hindu deity Shiva, who is believed to grant the desires of his devotees, hence the name 'Lord of the Quencher's Desire'. The name Sharwanand carries the meaning “Lord of the Quencher's Desire” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Sharwanand usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the quencher's desire and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the granting of desires and the attainment of spiritual bliss through devotion to Shiva.
data.etymology: Sharwanand belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Quencher's Desire.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sharwanand total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.
